scores.rationale: The stylized fact (SF6) is explicitly stated and catalogued in LoreMarq2010 [1], and supported by the DEB modeling discussion in [11]. The Zonneveld snippets [8] are the clearest physiological support: during light-limited growth the chlorophyll cell quota behaves oppositely to nutrient-limited growth, with chlorophyll production being light-dependent, consistent with chl:C decreasing as dilution/growth rate increases under light limitation. Snippets [4] and [6] corroborate the inverse chlorophyll-light relationship. One snippet [9] notes that the chlorophyll cell quota can still increase at low irradiance because growth dilution becomes less important — this nuances but does not clearly contradict the chl:C-vs-dilution-rate relationship, so it is the only mild counterpoint. Several other Zonneveld/Lorena snippets are topically related (about Chl:C usage, photoacclimation, or other stylized facts like SF8) but do not directly bear on this specific relationship. Overall there is moderate, multi-source support with little genuine conflict, hence corroborated.

scores.rationale: None of the snippets address the specific relationship between chlorophyll-to-carbon ratio (chl:C) and dilution (growth) rate under light-limiting conditions in chemostat/continuous culture. The stylized fact concerns photoacclimation dynamics where slower-growing (lower dilution rate) light-limited cells typically increase chl:C, whereas faster dilution decreases it. Several snippets touch on photosynthesis, chlorophyll content, and light acclimation (e.g., 1, 5, 7, 14, 17), but none report chl:C as a function of dilution/growth rate, and snippet 17 relates leaf chlorophyll to light availability rather than to dilution rate. No snippet provides direct supporting or contradicting evidence, so the corpus is essentially off-topic and offers insufficient evidence to evaluate the claim.
